# ADR-1092: Make uv.lock the only dependency source

## Status

accepted

## Context

Every pip install in the repository read one of thirteen committed
`requirements/*.txt` files that `scripts/generate_pip_constraints.py`
exported from `uv.lock` (ADR-0737, ADR-0775), and the plugin launcher kept a
third copy of its versions by hand in `scripts/launcher_pins.py` (ADR-0750,
ADR-0752), reconciled by a test. Dependabot's `pip` ecosystem treated the
exports as manifests and patched them line by line; its output can never
equal the generator's, so every Python Dependabot PR arrived red (#643,
#651, #652, #653) and needed a human resync commit. Re-running the lock
simulation of #653 on `main` reproduced both failure classes: the
generator's `--check` disagreed on 12 of 13 files, and once regenerated,
`test_launcher_pins_match_lock` failed on `mcp`, `psycopg`, `psycopg-pool`
and `sentence-transformers`. The owner decided on 2026-10-01 to delete the
duplication: `uv.lock` is the single source, nothing is paid for, and no
bot pushes to `main`.

## Decision

1. **CI and container images install with `uv sync --locked --inexact
   --no-install-project --no-default-groups <set>`**, through
   `.github/actions/uv-locked-install` in CI and the same command in
   `Dockerfile`, `docker/Dockerfile`, `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` and
   `.clusterfuzzlite/build.sh`. Each job keeps the extras/groups its file
   carried (the per-file headers of the deleted exports). `uv sync`
   verifies every artifact against the lock's sha256
   (`HashStrategy::from_resolution(..., HashCheckingMode::Verify)`,
   `crates/uv/src/commands/project/sync.rs:798` at uv 0.11.3).
   `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` points at the setup-python prefix, a venv or
   `/usr/local`, which uv documents as supported for CI and Docker
   (`docs/concepts/projects/config.md`, *Project environment path*, uv
   0.11.3) and never deletes when it is not a virtual environment
   (`crates/uv/src/commands/project/mod.rs`); `--inexact` keeps pip.
   `Verify` accepts a lock entry without a hash, so
   `tests_py/scripts/test_uv_lock_single_source.py` asserts every registry
   artifact in `uv.lock` has one.
2. **The launcher and both installers install from `uv.lock` too.**
   `scripts/launcher_uv.py` runs `uv export --frozen --format pylock.toml`
   for one set and `uv pip install --require-hashes --target <scratch>` on
   the result, then the existing scratch-and-commit path (ADR-1063,
   ADR-1064) moves it into `deps/`. A `pylock.toml` carries each wheel's URL
   and sha256, so the Linux `+cpu` torch needs no index flag and no second
   pin. The launcher's base and ML sets are the `launcher-base` and
   `launcher-ml` dependency groups in `pyproject.toml` (names only; adding
   them changed no locked version). Stamps are keyed on the sha256 of
   `uv.lock` and the interpreter's minor version.
3. **uv is bootstrapped, pinned and verified.** The launcher uses a `uv` on
   `PATH` only when it reports exactly `UV_VERSION` (0.11.3, the version CI
   already pinned); otherwise pip installs that wheel, binary-only and
   `--require-hashes` against the 19 sha256 PyPI serves for uv 0.11.3 (read
   2026-10-01 with `uv pip compile --generate-hashes --universal`), into
   `<deps>.uv-0.11.3` beside `deps/`. No prompt, no restart, no shell
   installer. A failure raises `UvUnavailableError` with pip's own error and the
   manual remedy; `scripts/setup.py` now stops on a failed install instead
   of printing a warning. Pinning matters because `uv pip install -r
   pylock.toml` is a preview feature in uv 0.11.3 (`--preview-features
   pylock`): the launcher never runs it under an arbitrary uv. The images
   copy the same uv from `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.11.3@sha256:90bbb3c1…`
   (index digest read 2026-10-01); the test above keeps CI, the images and
   the launcher on one version, which Dependabot does not bump (its docker
   parser reads `FROM` lines only).
4. **Dependabot uses the `uv` ecosystem on `/`.** Its updater runs `pyenv
   exec uv lock --upgrade-package <name>` and rewrites `pyproject.toml` and
   `uv.lock` together (`uv/lib/dependabot/uv/file_updater/lock_file_updater.rb`,
   dependabot-core `ea7cdf58`); with no `.txt`/`.in` file left at depth one,
   its fetcher finds nothing else to patch. github.com supports uv security
   updates (`data/reusables/dependabot/supported-package-managers.md`,
   feature `dependabot-uv-security-support`, github/docs `c008b66a`).
5. **Deleted:** `requirements/`, `scripts/generate_pip_constraints.py`,
   `scripts/pip_constraint_sets.py`, `scripts/launcher_pins.py`,
   `scripts/launcher_torch_cpu.py` and their tests, the Lint step
   `generate_pip_constraints.py --check`. `uv lock --check` stays.
   `requirements/fuzz.txt` had no reader: the ClusterFuzzLite build
   installed `ci-sqlite-min.txt`, and still installs that set.

## Consequences

Easier: a Dependabot Python PR edits only `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`,
which every job installs from directly, so nothing derived can disagree with
it. A clean-room install of each of the eleven installable sets through the
new command on macOS (Python 3.12/3.13) equals the old file's install
package for package, pip excepted; the `uv export` body of all thirteen
sets was byte-identical to the committed files, hashes included, before
they were deleted.

Easier: the launcher installs an exact, hash-checked closure instead of
letting pip resolve transitives from PyPI. Measured 2026-10-01, macOS
arm64, Python 3.13, cold caches: base set 32.0 s with pip, 7.4 s with uv
plus 8.1 s for the one-time uv bootstrap; ML set 175 s with pip, 64 s with
uv.

Harder: the plugin tree must ship `uv.lock` and `pyproject.toml` (it does;
the MCPB bundle does not use the launcher). The first launch without a
matching uv downloads uv once. A uv bump is a manual edit of four places
the test pins together, plus the 19 hashes.
